clue.text: Boozer, British, with soft drink turning up somewhere in Caribbean

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: soda is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A drinker at the pub, with a fizzy drink, somewhere in the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is British slang for a pub; 'turning up' reads the drink upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, so it is one example of a place there.

clue.text: Unable to speak outside home for a short time

indicators.note: the word for speechless sits outside, wrapping round the word for at home

parts.note: someone unable to speak is mute
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone struck dumb outside their house, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds, a standard example of a brief stretch of time.

clue.text: Counterfoil of cheque? Objections raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written from the bottom up

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A query about a cheque counterfoil, then some objections being voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a chequebook page left behind after the cheque is torn out is its stub; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Fleet member — 7 falling short

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: falling short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: the solution to 7 down, the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A member of a fleet, cross-referenced to another clue and coming up short.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer of 7 down, the first man; 'falling short' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Immoral collection of books appearing after a number of years

indicators.note: appearing after places the books' letters behind the stretch of years

parts.note: a decade is ten years
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Something immoral about a set of books published years later.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, so it is a synonym for immoral.

clue.text: Resistance met in a bogus retreat in India

indicators.note: met in means the resistance letter is found inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sham is something bogus, a fake
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition encountered at a fake spiritual retreat in India.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a hermitage or religious retreat in India, often centred on a guru.

clue.text: First person needing trailer in the morning

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film, an ad
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Somebody who comes first needs a film preview before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam was the first man created, hence the first person.

clue.text: A very odd riot involving a pilot

indicators.note: odd means the letters are made strange, jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very strange disturbance involving an airline captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' shuffles RIOT with the second A to give IATOR; 'involving' simply joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator flies aircraft, so the word is a dated synonym for a pilot.

clue.text: Moved gently and stopped, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Something moved carefully and then came to rest, after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the C off CEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something somewhere is to move it slowly and carefully, as when easing a car into a space.

clue.text: What's written to promote obscure book?

parts.note: to blur is to obscure, make indistinct

explanation.surface: A question about the copy written to sell a little-known book.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional description printed on a book's jacket.

clue.text: Puzzle for crossword solvers, perhaps starting point for trainspotting?

definitions.meaning: a rearrangement of letters, the staple puzzle of cryptic crosswords
the letters of 'starting point' can be rearranged to spell 'trainspotting', so one is an example of the other's rearrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzle for crossword fans, maybe how a train enthusiast's hobby begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like the origin of a hobby, but STARTING POINT and TRAINSPOTTING use exactly the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another is exactly what the second half describes.

clue.text: Pace back and forth to find where the stars are

indicators.note: back means the word for pace is read backwards

parts.note: pace means speed; read back it becomes the word for profound waters
forth means forwards, so the clue's own word pace is given again going forward

explanation.surface: Walk up and down to find out where the stars live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pace back' is SPEED written backwards, DEEPS; 'and forth' gives PACE itself read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the vast region of the universe beyond the Earth's neighbourhood, where the stars lie.

clue.text: Supports America over blemishes

indicators.note: over here means the blemish word is spread over, covering the abbreviation for America

parts.note: stains are blemishes
US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: Someone backs the United States despite its flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to hold up or bear the weight of, so it is a synonym for supports.

clue.text: Chief dismissing one fellow

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: main means chief, principal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boss sacks a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a chap or bloke, a male person, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Mention celebrities to impress? Pardon me — that's out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are not in their proper sequence, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for dropping famous names, admitting it was rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as a rebuke for bad manners but is the anagram signal for PARDON ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually in order to impress listeners.

clue.text: Concession that's very pleasing at first

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A concession that delights straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is something offered to placate or appease, a minor concession.

clue.text: When talking choose nice, but not last, piece of cake

indicators.note: when talking means the word for choose is only heard, so its spelling may differ

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: not last means the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: In conversation, opt for something nice, but not the last slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When talking' gives PIC, said like PICK; 'but not last' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a picnic and a piece of cake are idioms for something easy, so the second is a synonym.

clue.text: Plan to reject extremely good pastry dishes

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: mega is slang for extremely good
tarts are pastry dishes

explanation.surface: A scheme to turn down some excellent pies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ploy, a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: Comment about teacher's assessment

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a mark is the grade a teacher gives work

explanation.surface: A comment concerning the grade a teacher has given.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Piercing sound of bell at end of match

indicators.note: at end of places the bell's sound after the word for match

parts.note: to go is to match, as colours go together
a ring is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A shrill bell sounds as the game finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Goring is stabbing with horns, as a bull does, so it is a kind of piercing.

clue.text: Blurt out old demand

parts.note: ex means former, old
a claim is a demand for something owed

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out a long-standing demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so it is a synonym for blurting out.

clue.text: Cutting taken from sweet alyssums and others

indicators.note: a cutting taken from a plant is a piece of it, so the letters are a slice of the words

explanation.surface: A gardener takes a cutting from sweet alyssum plants and others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is gardening language for a slip of a plant, here a slice of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is the Latin abbreviation et alii, used in lists to mean and the rest.

clue.text: Fed up as soldiers kept in base?

indicators.note: kept in means the soldiers' letters are held inside

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as a road bed
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops confined to barracks are thoroughly fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bored means feeling weary and uninterested, which is what fed up describes.

clue.text: Sound made by outlawed group of musicians

indicators.note: sound made by means the word for outlawed is heard, not spelt

parts.note: outlawed means banned

explanation.surface: The noise produced by a prohibited group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians who play together.

clue.text: A small article about one from China, say

indicators.note: about means going round, so the other pieces surround the letter for one

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A short piece of writing about somebody from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is the adjective 'from China, say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from China is one example of something from Asia; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Came across criminal on train

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are behaving wrongly, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a crook while on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance, just like coming across them.
